title: India's Hockey World Cup 2026 Campaign Begins Friday: Full Schedule and Squad
excerpt: Harmanpreet Singh leads a 20-member squad into Pool D at the FIH Hockey World Cup in the Netherlands, with India facing Wales, England, and arch-rivals Pakistan in a bid to end a 51-year title drought.
body:
• India open their FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign against Wales on August 15 in Amstelveen, Netherlands, followed by England on August 17 and Pakistan on August 19.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh leads a 20-member squad blending veterans like Manpreet Singh with young talent, under chief coach Craig Fulton's "press, counter, perform" system.
  • India have not won a Hockey World Cup since 1975 — a 51-year drought the team aims to end at the Belgium-Netherlands co-hosted tournament running August 15-30.

India begin their quest to end a 51-year Hockey World Cup drought on Friday when Harmanpreet Singh leads a 20-member squad against Wales in their Pool D opener at the FIH Hockey World Cup Belgium & Netherlands 2026. The tournament, co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands, runs from August 15 to 30.

India are drawn in Pool D alongside England, Pakistan, and Wales, with all pool-stage matches scheduled at Amstelveen in the Netherlands. The group features a marquee clash against arch-rivals Pakistan on August 19, widely regarded as the most anticipated fixture of the pool stage.

Full Schedule (Pool Stage)

August 15: India vs Wales — Amstelveen, Netherlands

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2087912496967434380

August 17: India vs England — Amstelveen, Netherlands

August 19: India vs Pakistan — Amstelveen, Netherlands

Knockout rounds follow the pool stage, with the final scheduled for August 30.

Squad Breakdown

Hockey India announced the squad on July 21, naming a balanced group of experienced campaigners and in-form youth.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=gRHDVk4EB68

Goalkeepers: Mohith HS, Suraj Karkera

Defenders: Jarmanpreet Singh, Harmanpreet Singh (captain), Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Sanjay, Sumit, Yashdeep Siwach

Midfielders: Rajinder Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Hardik Singh, Manpreet Singh, Nilakanta Sharma, Vivek Sagar Prasad

Forwards: Dilpreet Singh, Shilanand Lakra, Sukhjeet Singh, Mandeep Singh, Abhishek

Key Players to Watch

Harmanpreet Singh — India's captain and ace drag-flicker is the team's most potent weapon from penalty corners. The defender has been one of world hockey's most consistent performers and carries the weight of India's title ambitions on his shoulders.

Manpreet Singh — India's most-capped player brings vast tournament experience to the midfield. His leadership and composure under pressure will be critical in tight knockout matches.

Hardik Singh — The dynamic midfielder provides the engine room energy and has been central to India's attacking play, linking defense to forward lines.

"This is a well-balanced squad — the right mix of tournament experience and in-form youth who've earned their spot through performance, not reputation."

— Craig Fulton, India chief coach

Coach Fulton's Philosophy

Chief coach Craig Fulton has built India's game around a clear tactical identity: "Press, counter, perform." The South African coach has emphasized that this is not just a tactical approach but a daily training mentality.

"We are not getting ahead of ourselves — one game at a time, all in, is the mentality we're taking into every match," Fulton said when the squad was announced.

India's World Cup History

India's last — and only — Hockey World Cup triumph came in 1975, when they won on home soil in Kuala Lumpur. Despite being one of hockey's most storied nations with eight Olympic gold medals, the World Cup title has eluded India for over five decades.

The tournament carries special significance for Indian hockey fans and the diaspora. With matches broadcast and streamed globally, millions of Indian fans across the US, UK, and Europe are expected to follow the campaign closely. The August 19 clash against Pakistan will draw particular attention from diaspora communities on both sides.

Where to Watch

The tournament will be broadcast on FIH's official platforms and partner broadcasters. In India, matches will be available on major sports networks. Fans in the US and Europe can access live streaming through FIH's digital channels.
